question.text: Mr. Anil Kumar's Cat II 'Saraswati Infra Debt Trust' is considering investing in Securitised Debt Instruments (SDIs). Per Chapter 9, SDIs were introduced by SEBI in __ under which regulation, and what is the defining feature of an SDI structure?

answer.text: 2008; SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations; an SDI is almost similar to an SPV that pools funds to invest in assets leasable to a target company, providing fixed lease-based income to investors.
2012; SEBI (AIF) Regulations; an SDI is a synthetic derivative linked to the Nifty-50.
2015; SEBI (REIT) Regulations; an SDI is a pass-through trust for listed real-estate rentals.
2020; SEBI (InvIT) Regulations; an SDI is a power-sector financing instrument only.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 9, SDIs were introduced by SEBI in 2008 under the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations. The workbook describes the SDI structure as almost similar to an SPV that pools funds and invests in assets that can be leased to a target company, generating fixed income for the investors — which is precisely what Option A states. The Trap: Options B, C and D pair the wrong year with the wrong regulation (AIF, REIT and InvIT regulations, respectively) and misdescribe the SDI structure. The 2008 SDI regulation is a discrete SEBI framework and is often confused with the later REIT/InvIT regimes. Note: The workbook does note that SDIs are rated by credit rating agencies, but it does not prescribe broader independent-lessor or compliance prescriptions in this passage; the question turns on identifying the correct year, regulation and structural description.
